events.title: Procedural crystal shards on every tile (highest impact)

events.description: Phase 1 implementation: chose hand-built 6-vertex/8-tri elongated octahedron mesh (vs. CreatePrimitive(Cube) scaled) because it reads more 'crystal shard' shape-wise and costs ~1/4 the vertex count. The mesh is built once and shared across every shard. Materials are bucketed into 5 gradient steps (inner→outer) and cached statically, so the entire cursed-area shard population batches into ~5 SetPass calls.

Phase 1: RNG seeded from `(uint)Entity.Index ^ (uint)Entity.Version | 1u` via Unity.Mathematics.Random (the `| 1u` guards the seed-0 invalid case). UnityEngine.Random is NOT used — lockstep peers will produce identical shard configurations.

events.title: Procedural crystal shards on every tile (highest impact)
events.notes: New file Assets/Scripts/Presentation/ProceduralCurseShardGenerator.cs (static class, Create(worldPos, tileEntity, em) entry). Modified Assets/Scripts/Presentation/PresentationSpawnSystem.cs lines ~350-360 to call the generator instead of returning an inactive GameObject. Each tile builds 4-6 elongated-octahedron shard GameObjects parented to a root; root has no collider so shards do not block click-selection. Shared 6-vertex mesh + 5 shared materials across the purple→green gradient (one material per bucket, not per tile). Reads OwnerNode + CrystalNode.SpreadRadius + LocalTransform off the node to drive the gradient; falls back to a 15 m radius if the node is missing. Determinism: seed = (uint)Index ^ (uint)Version | 1u via Unity.Mathematics.Random.

events.description: Phase 2: hero-light selection is `(tileEntity.Index % 10) == 0` AND `bucket <= 2` (the inner 3 of 5 gradient buckets). The modulo gate gives ~10% of tiles a light; the bucket gate confines lights to the inner half of the curse radius where they're visually meaningful. Combined, this caps the total hero-light count to roughly 15-25 per fully-spread node, comfortably under URP forward+'s per-camera light budget. No RNG — purely deterministic by Entity.Index, so lockstep peers see identical light placement.

Phase 2: bloom prerequisite is documented via a one-time `Debug.Log` (not LogWarning, to avoid spamming) on first shard spawn, gated by a static `_bloomNoticeFired` flag. We can't toggle URP Volume profiles from runtime code cleanly, so the notice asks the developer to verify Bloom is enabled in the active profile. Single fire per session keeps logs clean.

events.title: Hero-tile Point Lights (light emanation)
events.notes: Modified Assets/Scripts/Presentation/ProceduralCurseShardGenerator.cs only. Added hero-light branch at end of Create(): `(Entity.Index % 10) == 0 && bucket <= 2` selects roughly the inner 30% of tiles for a Point Light (type Point, range 2.5, intensity 1.5, shadows off, bounceIntensity 0, renderMode ForcePixel, localPos y=0.6 above the shard cluster). Light color sampled from the same purple→green gradient via new GetHeroLightColorForBucket(bucket) helper which lerps InnerEmission (#9B5BE0) → OuterEmission (#7AC83A) at bucket-centre t. Added one-time `Debug.Log` bloom prerequisite notice gated by `_bloomNoticeFired`. Determinism preserved — no UnityEngine.Random or Unity.Mathematics.Random in the hero-light path, just Entity.Index modulo + the static gradient-bucket value already computed for the shard material.

events.title: Ambient particle drift per crystal node

events.description: Phase 3 spawn hook: chose to attach the ParticleSystem inside CreateCrystalNodeVisual (in PresentationSpawnSystem.cs) gated by `presentationId == 310` (CrystalMainNode), rather than from CrystalSpreadSystem. CrystalSpreadSystem is a Burst ISystem and can't touch managed GameObject/ParticleSystem code. The PresentationSpawnSystem path runs exactly once per node (when its visual is first built), and parenting to the node root means cleanup is automatic when the node entity dies — no per-system tracking required. Sub-nodes (Resource/Enforcement/etc., PresentationIDs 312-316) deliberately do NOT get particles; they're visual accents, not curse-spread sources.

Phase 3 determinism note: ParticleSystem's built-in RNG (start position within the disc, exact velocity jitter, etc.) is NOT deterministic across peers. This is intentional and called out in the file header. Particles are purely cosmetic — no entity allocations, no commands, no gameplay impact. Lockstep does not care whether peer A's mote drifts 12cm left of peer B's. The shard placement (Phase 1) and hero-light placement (Phase 2) remain fully deterministic via Unity.Mathematics.Random seeded from Entity.Index.

events.title: Ambient particle drift per crystal node
events.notes: New file Assets/Scripts/Presentation/ProceduralCurseParticleGenerator.cs (static class, Create(nodePos, nodeEntity, em) entry). Modified Assets/Scripts/Presentation/PresentationSpawnSystem.cs CreateCrystalNodeVisual to spawn + parent a ParticleSystem under the main crystal node root when presentationId == 310. Particle params: emission 4/sec, lifetime 4s (~16 alive), startSpeed 0.3, velocityOverLifetime.y 0.4 (upward drift), startSize 0.05-0.15, disc shape sized to CrystalNode.SpreadRadius × 0.9 (fallback 15m), color gradient purple #9B5BE0 → green #7AC83A across lifetime with alpha 0→0.85→0 fade. Shared additive material + procedural 32×32 white radial-falloff texture cached statically so every node's particles batch. Particle GO parented to node root, so cleanup is automatic — when the node entity dies, the GO and its children are destroyed.

User chose 'Plan only — don't write code yet' for Iteration 2 (2026-05-21), same approach as the original task-111 creation. Task re-opened: status active, stage scope. Code lands in follow-up session after spec review.

Iteration 2 file naming: kept class + filename ProceduralCurseShardGenerator.cs stable rather than renaming to ProceduralCurseBlockGenerator.cs as the spec suggested. Same rationale as the existing 'BuildCommandPannel.cs (known misspelling, kept for reference stability)' convention in CLAUDE.md — file/class rename in Unity carries .meta migration risk and call-site churn for zero functional benefit. Internal geometry is now a voxel-block grid; the class header doc has been rewritten to reflect the Iteration 2 model.

Iteration 2 open-question resolutions: (Q1 z-fight) static HashSet<int2> _claimedCells with cluster-owned release on animator destroy. (Q2 animator allocation) one growth animator + one recession animator per cluster ROOT (NOT per block). Growth animator self-destructs after 1 s; recession animator stays dormant until BeginDeath() fires. (Q3 material reuse) per-block bucket assignment is fine — each block computes its own bucket from its cell's distance to the node, picks the matching shared material; SRP batcher still batches per material. (Q4 recession cleanup) PSS-checks-for-animator approach: CleanupDestroyedEntities checks for CurseBlockRecessionAnimator before calling Destroy(go); if present, calls animator.BeginDeath() and skips immediate destruction. The animator owns final cleanup.

Iteration 2 determinism strategy: per-cell heights hashed from integer world-grid coords (cellHash = (gx * 374761393u) ^ (gz * 668265263u) | 1u) via Unity.Mathematics.Random — NOT seeded per tile. This guarantees adjacent tiles' shared cells produce IDENTICAL heights, which is what makes the seam-tiling work. Hero-light selection still uses Entity.Index % 10. Particle RNG (growth burst, recession stream, ambient drift) is non-deterministic but cosmetic-only — same trade as Iteration 1 Phase 3.

Iteration 2 outward-flow implementation (item 6): added an inner CurseNodeAmbientDirector MonoBehaviour to ProceduralCurseParticleGenerator.cs. It polls CrystalSpreadState.CurrentRingRadius every 0.25 s via the EntityManager. While expanding (ring < SpreadRadius × 0.95), velocityOverLifetime.radial is set to OutwardFlowSpeed (1.6 m/s) and the emission shape.radius tracks the current ring radius so motes spawn near the frontier. Once spread is complete, falls back to the Iteration 1 gentle-upward-drift idle field.

events.description: Task task-cursed-ground-luminous-crystals-111 Iteration 2 (voxel-grid pivot) complete. Cursed-ground tiles now spawn as 5×5-ish voxel-block grids snapped to integer world coordinates so adjacent tiles tile seamlessly into one continuous block field — matching the SineVFX 'Living Particles' reference the user shared. Per-cell heights are hashed from integer cell coords so shared cells across tiles produce identical heights (multiplayer-safe, seam-stable). Cells are deduplicated via a static HashSet so adjacent tiles' overlapping cells don't z-fight. Each new block animates in over 1s with ease-out-back overshoot + a small particle burst at the top. When tiles recede, blocks animate down to 0 over 0.7s + emit a small inward particle stream toward the owning node. Per-node ambient particles now flow radially outward while the curse is still spreading (CrystalSpreadState.CurrentRingRadius < SpreadRadius × 0.95), idling to gentle upward drift once fully spread. Recession death-handoff: PresentationSpawnSystem.CleanupDestroyedEntities checks for CurseBlockRecessionAnimator before destroying the GO; if present, calls animator.BeginDeath() and skips immediate Destroy — the animator owns final cleanup. Material count and renderer estimate: 5 shared materials (one per gradient bucket) + 1 shared cube mesh (Unity primitive) → ~5 SetPass calls for the entire cursed-area block population, regardless of node count. Files: 3 modified (ProceduralCurseShardGenerator.cs full rewrite, ProceduralCurseParticleGenerator.cs outward-flow director, PresentationSpawnSystem.cs comment + death-handoff), 2 new (CurseBlockGrowthAnimator.cs, CurseBlockRecessionAnimator.cs). Also touched Assembly-CSharp.csproj to register the two new files for build verification (Unity will regenerate on next editor open).
